title: MCP Server Trust Review
summary: Review an MCP server's provenance, code path, identity, data access, tools, authorization, and containment before connection.
prerequisites: An identified server distribution or endpoint

sections.title: Review provenance and capability before connection
paragraphs: Confirm who publishes and operates the server, where its source or build comes from, how updates are signed or reviewed, and whether the endpoint or package matches the expected identity. Inventory the files, network destinations, APIs, tenant data, credentials, and external actions the server can reach under the actual runtime identity.

Review every exposed tool rather than trusting names or annotations. Determine whether it reads, writes, deletes, communicates externally, spends money, changes authorization, or operates across tenants. New tools must remain disabled until reviewed. A server update can change effective capability even when the connection name stays the same.

Keep record inspection separate from connection authority. RECORDS_MATCH means only that validated identity, tool, and network fields equal or are contained by their reviewed values. REVIEW_REQUIRED means at least one valid field differs or lacks supporting evidence. REJECT means the record is malformed or missing required fields. None of these inspection outcomes authorizes a connection.

The offline teaching program in this lesson consumes no actual trusted host-control evidence. It therefore always returns CONNECTION_BLOCKED_PENDING_VERIFICATION, even if every record matches and every claimed prerequisite flag is True. An authorized reviewer must validate containment, process policy, redaction, revocation, and other required evidence outside this toy before making any real operational decision.

code.label: Review outcomes
code.code:
Record inspection: RECORDS_MATCH | REVIEW_REQUIRED | REJECT
Connection decision from this offline toy: CONNECTION_BLOCKED_PENDING_VERIFICATION

RECORDS_MATCH is record equality or containment, not connection authority.
Claimed prerequisite flags are not trusted control evidence.
Only an authorized reviewer working outside this toy can evaluate real evidence.

sections.title: Record the trust decision
paragraphs: For remote servers, validate HTTPS, authorization-server metadata, audience-bound tokens, least-privilege scopes, redirect handling, and secret storage. For local servers, inspect the executable and launch arguments, then constrain filesystem, process, and network access. Never pass a client token through to an unrelated downstream service.

Use exact audience matching. In MCP, the audience identifies the MCP resource server, not an unrelated downstream API. OAuth discovery must be constrained to approved destinations because unconstrained discovery can create SSRF risk. These requirements follow the version-specific MCP authorization specification and MCP security best-practices documentation: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/authorization and https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/tutorials/security/security_best_practices.

This offline lesson records only CONNECTION_BLOCKED_PENDING_VERIFICATION. It has no approval-producing path and does not infer authority from Boolean claims, matching records, annotations, or simulated results. A real connection decision belongs to an authorized reviewer who can inspect independently generated evidence in the actual deployment.

If an organization later records conditions for reconsideration, those conditions describe work still to be completed. They do not constitute approval, and they must not be represented as permission to connect.

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: The expected evidence is a time-bounded decision tied to a specific server version or digest, exact endpoint, reviewed capability inventory, runtime identity, data policy, and containment test.

Evidence IDs that merely name a source, build, or update record do not establish a control. Without an excerpt binding the exact version and digest, the corresponding finding is UNKNOWN. An evidence record must include enough content to show what was inspected and what verdict was reached.

Verify denied scopes and destinations with safe probes, confirm tokens are audience-bound and absent from logs, exercise an approval-required tool without approving it, and confirm newly discovered tools stay disabled. Test disconnection, credential revocation, and recovery of dependent workflows. These procedures are not evidence that this lesson performed the tests.
Re-review after any server, owner, endpoint, tool inventory, scope, identity, or data-flow change. A changed digest or tool inventory requires a new review, even if the server name is unchanged.

sections.title: Worked case: fictional local catalog server
sections.callout: This is a synthetic inspection guide. It records evidence and simulated test results; it does not establish that a real signature, issuer, audience check, sandbox, or revocation control works.
paragraphs: Case: Acme Retail wants to connect a fictional local process named acme-catalog-mcp to an internal catalog database. The review target is version 1.4.2 with digest sha256:1111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111. The fictional publisher is Acme Retail Platform, and the fictional operator is the catalog-platform service team.

Inspect evidence artifacts by name. A PASS means the supplied record is internally consistent with the stated check. A FAIL means the record contradicts the required control. UNKNOWN means the record does not establish the control. In this case, the bundle names source, build, and update evidence IDs but supplies no underlying excerpts binding version and digest, so those findings are UNKNOWN.

The review is blocked. No connection is permitted until every preconnection condition listed in the decision is enforced by the responsible owner and recorded against this exact version, digest, runtime identity, and tool inventory.

code.label: Synthetic evidence bundle: local case

sections.title: Worked inspection: local record matching is not approval
paragraphs: REVIEW_REQUIRED, provenance and identity evidence: EV-SOURCE-LOCAL-001, EV-BUILD-LOCAL-001, and EV-UPDATE-LOCAL-001 are named, but no excerpts bind them to version 1.4.2 and the pinned digest. The result for that evidence is UNKNOWN, not PASS. A changed executable digest is FAIL and requires a new review.

RECORDS_MATCH, runtime and capability records: the supplied local identity, listed tools, and network destination match their corresponding pinned values. This is record inspection only. It does not prove that the host policy is enforced, that process creation is denied, or that the observed tool inventory is complete.

UNKNOWN, data, credentials, logging, timeout, containment, and rollback: the bundle states these controls, and some simulated results are recorded, but it does not contain independent authorized traces. The results remain UNKNOWN where enforcement or observation is required.

CONNECTION_BLOCKED_PENDING_VERIFICATION: the offline inspection cannot authorize the local connection. An authorized reviewer outside this toy must bind source and build evidence to the exact digest, verify the non-root runtime and host allowlists, confirm the tool-discovery trace, test approval-required export blocking, verify redacted logs, test timeout and fail-closed behavior, and test disable and database-role revocation. Claimed prerequisite flags, even if all are True, do not replace that evidence.

code.label: Local inspection record
code.code:
CHECK L-01 | identity record matches pinned name, version, and digest | RECORDS_MATCH | supplied identity fields
CHECK L-02 | source and build evidence bind the exact version and digest | UNKNOWN | EV-SOURCE-LOCAL-001, EV-BUILD-LOCAL-001 have no excerpts
CHECK L-03 | update path is independently reviewed | UNKNOWN | EV-UPDATE-LOCAL-001 has no underlying record
CHECK L-04 | listed tools are contained by reviewed inventory | RECORDS_MATCH | supplied tools and reviewed inventory
CHECK L-05 | network destinations are contained by allowlist | RECORDS_MATCH | supplied network fields
CHECK L-06 | filesystem, process, and network policy is enforced | UNKNOWN | simulated record is not live verification
CHECK L-07 | data policy and retention are evidenced | UNKNOWN | named evidence lacks an inspection excerpt
CHECK L-08 | credentials are least privilege and excluded from logs | UNKNOWN | enforcement and log trace required
CHECK L-09 | approval-required export is disabled without approval | UNKNOWN | simulated result is not live verification
CHECK L-10 | timeout and fail-closed behavior is verified | UNKNOWN | controlled test required
CHECK L-11 | revocation and recovery path is verified | UNKNOWN | authorized revocation trace required
INSPECTION SUMMARY | RECORDS_MATCH for validated identity, tool, and network fields only
CONNECTION DECISION | CONNECTION_BLOCKED_PENDING_VERIFICATION | this toy has no connection authority

sections.title: Contrasting case: fictional remote server
paragraphs: Case: A fictional remote endpoint, https://catalog.remote.example/mcp, reports version 2.0.0 and digest sha256:2222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222. The expected issuer is https://issuer.remote.example and the expected audience is mcp-catalog, identifying the MCP resource server. The observed audience is catalog-api, so the audience comparison fails. The issuer fields match in the supplied record.

The record also contains a redirect that is not an exact approved URI, does not establish a discovery-destination policy, and does not establish prohibition of token passthrough. The record-inspection outcome is REVIEW_REQUIRED. The connection decision is independently CONNECTION_BLOCKED_PENDING_VERIFICATION.

The reviewer must accept only tokens issued for the MCP server and must not pass a client token through to an unrelated downstream service. Token claims in this exercise are conceptual labels in a record, not real secrets or validated JWTs. No conclusion about cryptographic validity can be drawn from this synthetic evidence.

Even if the observed audience is changed to mcp-catalog and every prerequisite claim is changed to True, this toy may report RECORDS_MATCH but must still report CONNECTION_BLOCKED_PENDING_VERIFICATION. Actual authority requires an authorized reviewer to validate evidence outside the program.

    "offline record inspection has no connection authority"
  ]
}

sections.title: Evidence checklist for authorized sandbox verification
paragraphs: Use a dedicated test tenant, test database, synthetic records, and a host owned or explicitly authorized by the reviewer. Do not scan arbitrary public hosts. Do not use production credentials. Do not run destructive commands. A test result must identify the exact server version or digest, endpoint or executable, runtime identity, test time, tester, expected control, observed result, and retained redacted log reference.

Safe probes for a local server include reading an approved fixture, attempting to read a denied fixture path, attempting one denied network destination represented by a local test endpoint, invoking an approval-required tool without approval, stopping the process, and confirming that the dependent workflow fails closed. Safe probes for a remote server include requesting only approved OAuth metadata, checking an exact pre-registered redirect, requesting a deliberately insufficient scope in a test tenant, and confirming that a token for another audience is rejected. These are procedures to perform in an authorized environment, not claims that this lesson performed them.

For each probe, record whether the result is REAL_VERIFICATION, SIMULATED_EVIDENCE, or RECORD_INSPECTION. A simulated result must never be relabeled as an observed production control. Re-run the review after a server, owner, endpoint, tool, scope, identity, or data-flow change.

code.label: Verification evidence fields
code.code:
testId: unique identifier
scope: authorized host, tenant, endpoint, and synthetic data boundary
serverIdentity: exact version plus digest or commit
runtimeIdentity: user or service principal
expected: control being tested
probe: one safe, non-destructive action
observed: exact result, including denial or fail-closed behavior
classification: REAL_VERIFICATION | SIMULATED_EVIDENCE | RECORD_INSPECTION
logs: redacted event references, never secrets or bearer tokens
authorization: owner and approval record
cleanup: stopped process, removed fixture, revoked test credential if applicable
finding: PASS | FAIL | UNKNOWN
nextAction: retain, remediate, or reject connection

sections.title: Runnable offline exercise
sections.callout: The following Python program uses only the standard library and local fixtures. It has not been executed for this artifact. The expected output is derived by inspection of the code and fixtures.
paragraphs: Save the code as trust_review_exercise.py and run it with Python 3. It performs deterministic record inspection only. It performs no network access, OAuth exchange, cryptographic validation, process launch, filesystem probing, sandbox test, or trusted-host evidence collection.

The program validates nested values before comparison. Local pinned and observed identity fields must be nonempty strings. Expected and observed remote issuer and audience fields must be nonempty strings. Tool and network fields must be actual lists whose members are nonempty strings. Invalid JSON, missing fields, invalid nested values, unsupported deployment labels, and incorrect list types produce controlled REJECT outcomes rather than RECORDS_MATCH or an uncaught exception from the main inspection path.

Record inspection and connection authority are deliberately separate. Matching identity, tool, network, issuer, and audience records can produce RECORDS_MATCH. The connection_decision function has no branch based on records or prerequisite claims and always returns CONNECTION_BLOCKED_PENDING_VERIFICATION. An authorized reviewer must validate real control evidence outside this toy.

The standard-library behavior used here is documented at https://docs.python.org/3/library/json.html and https://docs.python.org/3/library/unittest.html. json.loads raises JSONDecodeError for invalid JSON, json.dumps with sort_keys=True sorts dictionary keys for deterministic serialization, and unittest.TestCase.assertEqual supplies the equality assertions.

code.label: Standard-library offline exercise

sections.title: Expected output and negative cases
paragraphs: The program has not been executed for this artifact. The following output is derived by inspection of the program's print statements and fixtures. The final FIXTURES line uses a placeholder rather than claiming an unobserved execution transcript. Its actual content is produced by json.dumps with sort_keys=True.
Expected main output representation:

LOCAL RECORDS_MATCH
LOCAL CONNECTION_BLOCKED_PENDING_VERIFICATION
REMOTE REVIEW_REQUIRED
REMOTE CONNECTION_BLOCKED_PENDING_VERIFICATION
NOTE no network, secrets, JWT validation, process launch, live containment test, or authority evidence consumed
FIXTURES {deterministic sorted JSON for the four named fixtures}
The unittest suite is separate from main output and runs when invoked with Python's unittest command. No passing-test count or actual execution result is claimed here.

The authority regressions cover both sides of record comparison. REMOTE_ALL_TRUE_MISMATCH has the original audience mismatch and all four prerequisite flags set to True. Its expected pair is REVIEW_REQUIRED and CONNECTION_BLOCKED_PENDING_VERIFICATION. REMOTE_ALL_TRUE_MATCH has matching issuer and audience fields and the same True flags. Its expected pair is RECORDS_MATCH and CONNECTION_BLOCKED_PENDING_VERIFICATION. Both tests also assert that the decision text does not contain APPROVE.

Other negative cases include a changed local digest, an unreviewed catalog_write tool, an issuer mismatch, malformed JSON, missing top-level fields, an empty nested identity field, a scalar tools value, an empty tool name, a non-string network member, and an empty audience. Malformed cases are expected to return controlled REJECT inspection outcomes and the blocked connection decision.

The program does not decide whether a host policy is genuinely enforced. It does not validate a signature, JWT, issuer metadata document, redirect, sandbox, revocation event, or live network boundary. Those checks require authorized verification outside the toy.

code.label: Commands and expected regression results
code.code:
python trust_review_exercise.py
python -m unittest trust_review_exercise.py

Expected main decision lines:
LOCAL RECORDS_MATCH
LOCAL CONNECTION_BLOCKED_PENDING_VERIFICATION
REMOTE REVIEW_REQUIRED
REMOTE CONNECTION_BLOCKED_PENDING_VERIFICATION

Regression fixture: REMOTE_ALL_TRUE_MISMATCH
Inspection: REVIEW_REQUIRED
Connection: CONNECTION_BLOCKED_PENDING_VERIFICATION
Reason: audience differs even though every prerequisite claim is True

Regression fixture: REMOTE_ALL_TRUE_MATCH
Inspection: RECORDS_MATCH
Connection: CONNECTION_BLOCKED_PENDING_VERIFICATION
Reason: matching records and True claims do not supply independent authority evidence

No actual execution or passing-test count is claimed.

sections.title: Independent changed-input task
sections.callout: Complete this task before reading the answer key. Distinguish record matching from connection authority, and do not treat annotations or Boolean claims as authorization.
paragraphs: A new local record keeps the server name acme-catalog-mcp but changes the digest to sha256:3333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333. Its discovered tools are catalog_search, catalog_get, and catalog_write. catalog_write can modify product prices and requires approval according to its description. The pinned review contains only catalog_search and catalog_get. The host policy still lists only catalog-db.internal.example:5432, but no evidence shows that the write operation is restricted to a test tenant.

Separately, a remote record has expected issuer https://issuer.remote.example and expected audience mcp-catalog, but observed issuer https://other-issuer.example and observed audience catalog-api. The record includes an annotation saying trusted=true. It also says a client access token may be passed to a downstream billing API. Treat the token as conceptual. Do not attempt to decode or validate a real token.

Task: produce a separate record-inspection outcome and connection decision for each record. Name failed and unknown checks, identify the evidence required, state that the new write tool must remain disabled, identify the identity and audience problems, and specify minimum conditions, owner, expiry, and remaining restrictions for any future review. This offline exercise must not grant connection approval under any input.

code.label: Changed-input task fixture

sections.title: Answer key and actionable feedback
paragraphs: Local record inspection: REVIEW_REQUIRED. The digest mismatch is FAIL and requires source or build evidence bound to sha256:3333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333. The additional catalog_write tool is outside the pinned reviewed inventory, so tool containment is FAIL. The stated network value matches the stated allowlist, but that equality does not prove enforcement. The absent test-tenant restriction evidence is UNKNOWN. The write tool must remain disabled.

Local connection decision: CONNECTION_BLOCKED_PENDING_VERIFICATION. The True prerequisite claims do not establish authority. Required external evidence includes a new source and build review for the changed digest, an explicit review of the price-changing tool, approval and authorization controls, idempotency and rollback analysis, test-tenant enforcement, host-enforced destination and filesystem restrictions, redacted audit evidence, and authorized containment and revocation traces. Owner: the designated security owner. Expiry: UNKNOWN until that owner records a dated review. Remaining restrictions: no connection, no write tool, no customer data, no public-network access, no unreviewed tools, and no arbitrary filesystem or process access.

Remote record inspection: REVIEW_REQUIRED. The issuer mismatch is FAIL. The audience mismatch is FAIL because catalog-api is not the expected MCP resource audience mcp-catalog. The trusted=true annotation is not authority. The stated downstream token passthrough conflicts with MCP security guidance and requires remediation. Exact redirect validation, constrained discovery destinations, and least-privilege scopes remain UNKNOWN because the fixture supplies no evidence for them.

Remote connection decision: CONNECTION_BLOCKED_PENDING_VERIFICATION. The True prerequisite claims do not change that result. Required external evidence includes exact issuer and MCP-resource audience validation, exact pre-registered redirect validation, prohibition of token passthrough, constrained discovery destinations, least-privilege scopes, and independent gateway or host evidence. Owner: the designated remote-service security owner. Expiry: UNKNOWN until a dated review is recorded. Remaining restrictions: no remote connection, no downstream token forwarding, no unreviewed scopes, no unapproved redirects, and no unverified discovery destinations.

Neither answer may claim that cryptography, JWT validation, sandboxing, host enforcement, or live revocation was performed. The same separation of record equality from independent authority applies regardless of model provider or deployment. Model-family selection does not establish MCP server security. The host and server stack must supply evidence to an authorized reviewer.

sections.title: Official procedures and transfer notes
paragraphs: Use the official version-specific MCP authorization specification for authorization-server metadata, protected-resource authorization, scopes, token handling, and the MCP resource audience: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/authorization. This URL is version-specific and is not described here as the latest specification.

Use the official MCP security best-practices documentation for exact redirect validation, accepting only tokens issued for the MCP server, prohibition of token passthrough, OAuth discovery SSRF considerations, local-server compromise, and scope minimization: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/tutorials/security/security_best_practices.

The supplied research also identifies Anthropic MCP connector documentation at https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-connector. That source is a provider-specific operational note, not evidence that another provider or deployment enforces the same controls. Transfer the checklist only after inspecting the other deployment's host policy, server implementation, identity, permissions, logs, and recovery controls.

A missing source, contradictory digest, unexpected tool, malformed nested value, issuer or audience mismatch, unverified redirect, possible token passthrough, absent destination allowlist, or untested containment control must be recorded as FAIL, UNKNOWN, or REJECT according to the evidence. Matching records and claimed Boolean prerequisites must never be converted into connection authority by this offline program.

Python JSON parsing, deterministic sorted serialization, and unittest assertions are documented at https://docs.python.org/3/library/json.html and https://docs.python.org/3/library/unittest.html. The exercise uses only those standard-library facilities and makes no claim that its tests were executed.
